body_text:
Two formulas $\varphi$ and $\psi$ are *logically equivalent*,
written $\varphi \equiv \psi$ or $\models \varphi \iff \psi$,
when they receive identical truth values under every common
interpretation and variable assignment.

Logical equivalence is a metalogical relationship between
sentences; it licenses the substitution of equivalents in any
extensional context without altering the truth value of the
enclosing formula. It must not be conflated with the object-
language equality relation $x = y$, which asserts that two
syntactic names designate the same entity within a domain.
